comments.content: getAdapter for InputStream returns file.getContents() which must be closed by the caller. The current implementation throws RuntimeException on CoreException, which is abrupt and loses Eclipse error context; consider logging and returning null or wrapping in a domain exception instead of an unchecked RuntimeException.

InputStream obtained via node.getAdapter(InputStream.class) is used without ever being closed. Files.copy(InputStream, Path) does not close the stream, so the Eclipse file contents stream leaks. Use try-with-resources and close the stream after copying.

copyInputStream does not close the InputStream it receives and Files.exists can throw IOException which is not handled. The method should close the stream in a finally block / try-with-resources and handle IO errors instead of letting them propagate unchecked.
